# Psalm 90 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A prayer of Moses, the man of God. Lord, you have been our home from one generation to the next.

**2** Before the mountains existed, before you gave birth to the earth and the world — from the beginning of time to the end of time — you are God.

**3** You turn people back to dust, saying, 'Go back to what you came from, children of Adam.'

**4** A thousand years mean nothing to you — they're like yesterday once it's over, like a few hours in the night.

**5** You sweep people away like a flood while they sleep. They're like grass that springs up in the morning —

**6** it's green and growing at dawn, but by evening it's dried up and dead.

**7** We're worn down by your anger; your fury leaves us terrified.

**8** You've spread out all our sins right in front of you — even our secret ones are exposed in the light of your face.

**9** All our days slip away under your displeasure; our years end with nothing but a whisper.

**10** We get maybe seventy years — eighty if we're strong — and even the best of those years are filled with struggle and heartache. Life goes by so fast, and then we're gone.

**11** Who truly grasps the force of your anger? Your fury matches the reverence you deserve.

**12** Teach us to make the most of our days so that we may develop a wise heart.

**13** Come back to us, LORD! How much longer? Show compassion to those who serve you.

**14** Drench us with your faithful love in the morning so we can sing for joy and be happy for the rest of our lives.

**15** Give us joy to match the years of suffering — equal to the time we've experienced hardship.

**16** Let your servants see what you can do! Let their children witness your majestic power!

**17** May the kindness of the Lord our God rest on us. Make the work of our hands count for something — yes, make our work truly matter!

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **90:1-2**: This is the Bible's most majestic meditation on eternity. Before anything existed — before mountains, before the earth — God was already God. And he'll still be God when everything else is gone.

- **90:10-12**: 'Seventy years — eighty if we're strong.' And even those years are full of struggle. The prayer that follows — 'teach us to number our days' — is one of the most practical requests in Scripture. Wisdom starts with knowing you won't live forever.

- **90:17**: After all the heavy theology about eternity and mortality, the psalm ends with something surprisingly simple: 'Make our work matter.' That's what we all want — to know that the brief time we have actually counts for something.

— PNEUMA
